samples.summary: PDF/file editor reaches the same data-loss path with neither guard registered
samples.evidence: The new guard is registered only by `SyncStatusChip` (packages/frontend/src/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.tsx:115), and the chip is mounted only where `SiteHeader` gets `syncStatus` — document-detail.tsx:654, slides-detail.tsx:411/797, docs-detail.tsx:199, board-detail.tsx:162, notes-detail.tsx:262 — plus `SharedHeaderStatus`. The owned PDF route mounts `SiteHeader` WITHOUT `syncStatus` (packages/frontend/src/app/files/file-shell.tsx:108) while `PdfCollabProvider` attaches a real Yorkie document that is written on comment add/reply/resolve (packages/frontend/src/app/files/comments/pdf-comment-store.ts:122,158,167,177,195). So a PDF comment made while disconnected is discarded by a sidebar click with no prompt — neither `beforeunload` nor the new navigation guard covers it. This is acknowledged as intentional at packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:734-740 ("PDF is uniformly out of scope"), which is why it is filed as minor rather than major, but the guard's own comment claiming coverage "follows this component" hides that a sixth writable CRDT surface exists outside it.

samples.summary: `go` passthrough leaves browser/programmatic back as an unguarded exit from an editor with unsent edits
samples.evidence: `go: (delta) => base.go(delta)` is unwrapped, so any `navigate(-1)` and the browser Back button unmount `DocumentProvider` and drop the change queue silently — the exact loss the push guard exists to prevent. Today no app code calls `navigate(-1)` (grep over packages/frontend/src found no `navigate(-1)` / `.go(` outside the provider itself), so the reachable bypass is the browser's own back button; it is documented as a known limitation in docs/design/sync-status.md:355-359 and 463-467. Filed so the gap is weighed rather than assumed closed.

samples.summary: The redirect latch is shared with `logout()`, whose redirect can now be superseded 2s later
samples.evidence: `redirectTo` has a second caller, `logout()` at packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:108, which sends the browser to "/". Previously the latch was permanent, so whichever redirect started first was the only assignment to `window.location.href` for the life of the tab. With the 2s release, a logout navigation that has not yet committed (slow document unload, or a `beforeunload` prompt from the sync guard the user is still reading) can be overwritten by a later 401's `redirectTo("/login")`, landing the user somewhere other than the destination the first navigation chose. Impact is a wrong landing page, not data loss; the new test only covers the /login path (packages/frontend/tests/api/auth.test.ts).

samples.summary: Design doc still asserts no `beforeunload` handler exists in the frontend
samples.evidence: docs/design/sync-status.md:249 states "There is no `beforeunload` handler anywhere in `packages/frontend/src` today, so nothing conflicts", while packages/frontend/src/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.tsx:101 registers one (and this change now hangs the navigation guard off the same condition). The claim reads as a live statement about the tree and is no longer true; a future guard author checking for conflicts would be misled.
